To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
EGF induces the synthesis of uPA and its cell surface expression, and the induction of uPA is mediated by the EGF receptor and is not dependent on the presence of the uPA receptor.
EGF enhances cell surface uPA activity and uPA-R expression, and that this effect can be blocked by cyclohixamide.
EGF induces uPA activity on the surface of A431 cells and that this induction is dependent on the number of EGF-receptors on the cell surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of EGF induced changes in uPA activity in A431 cells.
the regulation of uPA activity in A431 SqCC cells and the influence of EGF and its receptor on uPA-Rs.
the mechanism by which epidermal growth factors (EGFs) regulate the synthesis and secretion of uPA in squamous carcinoma cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EGF regulates cell surface uPA in a concentration dependent, time dependent, and protein synthesis dependent manner in a cell line which possesses a high density of cell surface EGF receptors.
EGF induces uPA activity by increasing the number of receptors on the cell surface.
uPA is a cell membrane protein which is regulated by EGF.

EGF enhances the expression of uPA-R in human squamous carcinoma cells and that EGF enhances uPA binding to its receptor.
